g.text: Fast · Temporary · Erased when power off
extra space when RAM is full
1. RAM is fast primary memory - holds active programs, but is erased when power off.
2. Storage (HDD, SSD, NVMe) is slower but permanent and much larger.
3. When RAM fills up, OS moves less-used data to a Virtual Memory area on storage.
4. This frees space in RAM so active programs keep running smoothly.
5. Virtual memory is slower than real RAM - it is a helper, not a replacement.
